ar_wall_of_things.blurb: Wall of Things is the first cliff you meet on the hike into Horn Mountain, off to the left in the Richland Creek country of north-central Arkansas. A line of bolts running up and over a roof roughly 20 to 25 feet off the ground makes the wall easy to spot. It has eight climbs, nearly all of them bolted sport routes plus one more, in the moderate to intermediate range from 5.9 to 5.10c. The cliff suits a party looking for a short session of solid mid-grade leads rather than anything hard or long.

_expect.name: FMO Wall (aka F@&K Mike O Wall)

ar_fmo_wall_aka_f_k_mike_o_wall.blurb: This is a small sport wall in the Piney Bowl pocket of the Big Piney region, north-central Arkansas. Reach it by going beyond the Main Wall and dropping a few steps to a lower belay ledge; it is the leftmost wall in that part of the bowl. All eight routes are bolted and hard: most fall in the 5.12 range, with a pair at 5.11 and one at 5.13. It is a destination for people already climbing in the upper grades, not a place to warm up or bring a beginner.

ar_mother_in_law_boulder.blurb: A leaning block in the N Forty Boulders on the north side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, north-central Arkansas, sitting up the slope from the Honeycomb boulder. Problems start on its west and south faces. There are eight in all, spanning VB-level warm-ups up to V6, with a cluster around V2 and another around V5. The lines are enjoyable, though the finishes on top of the block are awkward and worth scouting before you commit. It is also known as Toilet Bowlder.

ar_kindergarten_boulder.blurb: A big freestanding boulder at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, down the slope from the Groovy Area and among the first large detached blocks you come to on the way to the North Forty. Bolted sport and trad lines cover all four of its faces, alongside boulder problems from VB up to about V4. Routes here are mostly short and moderate, around 5.7 to 5.8, though the boulder as a whole holds climbs from 5.2 into the 5.12s. The north face is the one suggested for newer climbers.

ar_plaque_wall_the.blurb: The Plaque Wall is on the southeast side of the Throne area at Sam's Throne in north-central Arkansas, part of the main bluffline rather than the freestanding Throne itself. It faces southeast, so expect a fair amount of sun. Most of its eight lines are trad, with one sport route and one aid line, and the grades run from 5.7 up to a very hard 5.13. The climbing centres on a raised ledge under an overhanging crack and a roofed ledge about halfway up. A gully on the left can be walked up to set top ropes.

ar_nipple_stimulation_alcove.blurb: A compact alcove in the Middle East section of the East Side at Horseshoe Canyon Ranch, north-central Arkansas. It sits to the right of the tool buttress, only a short walk right of a gully. Eight climbs, split evenly between sport and trad, with a few also usable on top rope. Grades stay in a narrow band, from the 5.7s through 5.9 on the trad lines to 5.10 on the bolted ones, so it works well for a mixed party that wants moderate routes in one spot.
